chunk_findings.detail: The added branch still treats any ancestor of HEAD as a valid `--reviewed-sha` once the branch has no commits of its own. `merge-base --is-ancestor full head` is true for every commit in base history when head is at base, and nothing checks that `full` is that item's merged commit. The new test demonstrates it: T1 is claimed onto a branch at base and `--reviewed-sha` is `m1`, an older commit that was never T1's landing; standards records passed and stores that sha. chunk_findings.detail: The new implement waiver treats any resolvable `reopened_merge` object as “already implemented”. `W.rev(wt, it.reopened_merge)` only checks that the object exists in the repo, not that it is an ancestor of the worktree base. After a re-claim whose fresh tree is at a base that does not contain that landing (gitflow or stacking merge onto another branch, or main rewritten so the old merge commit is no longer in HEAD but still in the object store), the commit-ahead count is 0 and this branch still returns `""`, so `gate record implement --outcome passed` succeeds for work that is not in the tree about to merge. The standards waiver at the new `W.rev(where, prior) == full` check has the same hole: it accepts that sha as `--reviewed-sha` without `merge-base --is-ancestor`. The regression test never builds a base that lacks `prior`, so it stays green.

chunk_findings.detail: The standards exception treats any `reopened_merge` that is an ancestor of the live branch head as the reviewed commit, and it never checks that the branch still has no commits ahead of base. After a merged item is re-claimed (so `reopened_merge` is the prior landing L and the branch sits on main), commit a new change C on that branch and run `gate record standards --reviewed-sha L`. L is still an ancestor of head C and equals `reopened_merge`, so this block returns success and records L, even though C was not reviewed. The following refusal ("What merges is not what was reviewed") is skipped, so unreviewed post-reclaim commits can pass standards. The NOTE even claims the head has no commit ahead of base without testing that.

chunk_findings.detail: The standards exception only requires zero commits ahead of `base`, plus `reopened_merge` equal to the reviewed sha and an ancestor of `head`. It never snapshots the base at re-claim and never clears `reopened_merge` when later commits land, so “not ahead” is also true after those commits have been absorbed into `base`. Re-claim with `reopened_merge=L` and head at main, commit `C` on the item branch, fast-forward main to `C` so `base==head==C`. `base..head` is empty, `L` is still an ancestor of `head`, and `gate record standards --reviewed-sha L` takes the new success return and records `L`. `C` is what head actually is, and it was not the reviewed sha. The ahead-count probe does not cover this interleaving.

chunk_findings.detail: The standards waiver still accepts a prior landing after that landing has been reverted, as long as the branch has not moved off the recorded fork. Re-claim with `reopened_merge=L` and `head == base_sha` (contains `L`); main then gains `R`, a revert of `L`. `base..head` is empty, `head == rev(base_sha)`, `rev(L) == full`, and `L` is still an ancestor of `head`, so `--reviewed-sha L` returns success. Merging that branch into main is a no-op and leaves `R`'s tree, so the reviewed landing is not what will merge.

chunk_findings.detail: The implement waiver still treats “prior landing content equals this worktree HEAD” as “the landed work is what would merge.” `_prior_landing_here` ignores `base` and only runs `git diff --quiet <reopened_merge> HEAD -- globs`. Given a re-claim whose worktree HEAD is the recorded fork `F` (contains landing `L`), then main gains `R` (a revert of the declared paths) while the worktree stays at `F`: `base..HEAD` is empty, the diff against HEAD is quiet, and implement returns success. Merging that branch is a no-op and leaves `R`’s tree, so the item is marked implemented when the landing is no longer on main and will not be restored.
